newsitem.title: USA: Leonard Katzman, producer of TV's "Dallas," dies.
newsitem.headline: Leonard Katzman, producer of TV's "Dallas," dies.

text.p: The funeral of Leonard Katzman, executive producer of the CBS television series "Dallas," took place Sunday, a spokeswoman for Mt. Sinai Mortuary said.
She said Katzman died Thursday at his Malibu home at the age of 69. News reports gave the cause of death as a heart attack.

"Dallas," the story of a wealthy Texas family, aired from 1978 to 1991 and achieved blockbuster ratings with its focus on money, sex and power. It attracted international attention when its central character, the conniving J. R. Ewing (Larry Hagman), was shot as a season-ending cliffhanger.

Katzman produced, directed and wrote hundreds of "Dallas" episodes. But he had made his name in television long before, working on such series as "Playhouse 90," "The Alcoa Hour," "Route 66," "Gunsmoke," "Hawaii Five-O" and "The Wild, Wild West."
A native of New York, he attended Fairfax High School in Los Angeles. He is survived by his wife, LaRue, sons Frank and Mitchell, and six grandchildren.
